context: AnchorHEC is a targetless hand-eye calibration method for jointly calibrating a robot wrist camera and fixed cameras, without calibration targets. The approach uses reconstructed wrist-camera poses and forward-kinematics information, with FK-selected image pairs, confidence-based weighting, and a robust objective for the initial estimate. For fixed cameras, it pools reconstructed 2D–3D correspondences, estimates camera poses using RANSAC PnP and nonlinear refinement, and applies an ambiguity rejection rule; unsupported or rejected registrations fall back to a corrected shared-reconstruction-frame pose. Experiments used DUSt3R, MASt3R, VGGT, and ViPE reconstructions, with five trials, 15 wrist poses, and five fixed-camera frames unless otherwise stated. The excerpt reports translation error et and geodesic rotation error eθ, though their units are not shown in the supplied text. With the default VGGT backbone and 15 wrist poses, AnchorHEC (“Ours”) obtained wrist-camera errors of et=2.98 and eθ=0.41 in the room scene, and et=1.02 and eθ=0.22 on the tabletop. For fixed cameras, the corresponding errors were et=1.79 and eθ=0.32 in the room, and et=0.66 and eθ=0.19 on the tabletop. The reported real-world table contains ROC-AUC values: SAFE-LSTM achieves 77.27 and SAFE-MLP 86.76 on seen and unseen π0-FAST Franka tasks, while on OpenVLA WidowX they achieve 84.29 and 89.11 on seen tasks and 71.80 and 88.42 on unseen tasks, respectively. A conformal-prediction band Cα is calibrated on seen evaluation data; an upper threshold δt is then used, with a failure flagged when the score st exceeds δt.
